Based on the search results, here's a comprehensive comparison of Carbon vs Oxide for Rust in 2026:

## Overview

Carbon and Oxide (uMod) are the two main modding frameworks for Rust dedicated servers that allow you to run plugins which add features, manage players, and customize gameplay. For nearly a decade, if you wanted to run a modded Rust server, you had one option: Oxide (uMod), which was the industry standard and the backbone of the community.

## Performance

A key difference is performance. Carbon uses a modern technique called Dynamic Hooking that hooks into the game code more intelligently and efficiently, with Carbon servers often booting 30-40% faster than equivalent Oxide servers. In contrast, Oxide works by patching the game's DLLs extensively, which can sometimes lead to slower server startup times and "garbage collection" spikes.

## Plugin Compatibility

Carbon's robust framework and backward compatibility with Oxide plugins make it the ultimate replacement for those wanting better functionality and performance from their plugins. Carbon is a modern framework with 30-40% faster boot times and ~99% Oxide cross-compatibility.

## Recommendations for 2026

Oxide wins on historical stability and catalog; Carbon wins on performance and new features, and for new servers in 2026, many choose Carbon. However, for servers already running Oxide without issues, there's no urgency to migrate.
